title: Day 673 — US Suspends Avocado Export Inspections in Michoacán Over Threat to Inspectors
detail: On August 5, 2026 (Day 673, Wednesday), the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) halted phytosanitary inspections required for Mexican avocado exports in Michoacán, citing an unspecified 'threat against U.S. interests' after inspectors received threats in the field. The suspension immediately froze new certifications needed to ship avocados to the United States, Mexico's overwhelming top export market (roughly 90% of Mexican avocado exports by volume, worth $3.65 billion in 2025). Michoacán supplies 75-80% of Mexico's total avocado output and the industry directly employs over 200,000 people in the state. It marked the third U.S. suspension of Michoacán avocado inspections since 2022, all tied to security incidents against American inspectors. Michoacán Governor Alfredo Ramírez Bedolla said the pause was intended to safeguard inspectors following recent security incidents and extortion-related arrests in the region.
